lead: Lakewood plumbing deals with cold snaps, expansive soils and 1950s and 1960s ranch homes. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Lakewood.
risk: frozen pipes and sprinkler lines, sewer lines cracked by shifting soil and basement water heaters
risk_short: frozen pipes, sewer lines and water heaters
why: Much of Lakewood was built in the 1950s and 1960s, so many ranch homes have galvanized supply lines and clay or cast-iron sewer laterals. Expansive clay in parts of the city cracks those lines.
Cold fronts freeze sprinkler systems, hose bibs and pipes near exterior walls. Many homes have basements with water heaters and floor drains.
utility: Denver Water and local water districts
water: Much of Lakewood gets water from Denver Water, which uses mountain snowmelt. Some areas are served by local districts. The water is generally soft.
tips: Blow out sprinkler lines before the first hard freeze.
Scope the sewer line before buying an older home.
Test your sump pump each spring.
areas: PipeMend works in Belmar, Green Mountain, Bear Creek, Lakewood Heights, Eiber, Morse Park, Union Square and every other Lakewood neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Lakewood Building Division, and plumbers must be licensed through the Colorado State Plumbing Board.

faq.a: Many Lakewood homes get water from Denver Water, and others from local water districts. Your water bill shows which one serves you.
